$comment: WHAT THIS FILE CAN AND CANNOT DO. Read this before adding anything to it, because eleven
days and five fixes were spent on the assumption that it could do more than it can.
IT CANNOT GRANT PERMISSIONS TO A SCHEDULED CLOUD RUN. Measured on 2026-08-30, not reasoned
about. The file IS loaded there: the diagnostics log reports four settings sources and no
errors. Its permission grant is simply inert, because a CLONED REPOSITORY IS NOT PERMITTED
TO GRANT ITSELF bypassPermissions. If it were, cloning any repository would be arbitrary
privilege escalation, so this is a security property and not a bug to route around. The only
grant in force in that session came from the host's own launcher settings, which allowed one
tool. `defaultMode` and `allow` below apply where the host honours them, which in practice
means a maintainer session at a keyboard. Treat them as a convenience, never as the thing
keeping an unattended run alive.
SO EVERY WRITE PROMPTS IN A SCHEDULED RUN, whatever tool makes it and wherever it lands. A
shell redirect, a Write call, and an ordinary file in the working tree were tested
side by side on 2026-08-30 and all three prompted. Nothing in this file changed that and
nothing in this file can.
AND A SESSION CANNOT SEE THAT IT PROMPTED. The tool result reads `File created successfully`
whether it was auto-approved or a human tapped approve on a phone an hour later. This is the
reason the same defect shipped five times under five different fixes: every run verified its
own fix, honestly, and was wrong. A run record claiming 'no prompt' is unevidenced. No run
can know.
WHAT ACTUALLY FIXED IT, and the shape of the fix is the part worth keeping. The routine used
to declare its lane by writing `.git/ACTOR` at Phase 0 and twice more around the retro. Five
fixes were tried and every one of them aimed at HOW that file was written: an allow list of
exact command strings, then more strings, then the compound forms an entry could not match,
then a prose rule against chaining, then the Write tool. The fifth was a different KIND of
fix from the four before it and it failed the day after it shipped, because the diagnosis
under all five was the same and it was wrong.
The dependency was removed instead. The branch already named the lane, and CI had judged
commits that way since 2026-08-16, so the file was carrying information nothing needed it to
carry. `resolve_actor()` in scripts/shared/ownership_check.py now reads TXDOCKET_ACTOR, then
a stamp file if some other process left one, then the branch prefix, then `human`. A phase
wanting a narrower lane rides the commit it is already making, with
`TXDOCKET_ACTOR=upgrade git commit`, which costs no extra tool call. Nothing is written and
there is nothing left to approve. scripts/shared/actor_stamp_shape.py fails the build if any
instruction file goes back to requiring the write.
THE GENERAL RULE, which is what to carry to the next one of these: a rule that makes an
unattended run depend on a permission it cannot grant itself is not fixable by rewording the
rule, by enumerating command strings, or by changing which tool makes the call. Remove the
dependency. If a step genuinely cannot avoid a write, it needs the HOST configured to allow
it, and that is a change to the environment rather than a change to this file.
THE ALLOW LIST BELOW IS BELT AND BRACES AND NOTHING MORE. It is every tool a run uses rather
than the handful somebody remembered, because a list of what somebody remembered is not a
list of what a run does. `mcp__github` is server wide because this routine reads checks,
opens a pull request and merges it, and the useful set is not enumerable in advance.
GMAIL IS LISTED TOOL BY TOOL AND `send_message` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. These routines DRAFT
ONLY and never send, which CLAUDE.md states twice and the routine states again at Phase 19.
A server wide Gmail entry would quietly hand a run the ability to send mail on the owner's
behalf, and the one rule this project will not risk to save four lines of config is that
one. The absence is the point. Do not replace these four entries with `mcp__Gmail`.
`additionalDirectories` names the harness scratch root, where the harness itself writes
subagent transcripts. Run scratch belongs in `out/<run>/tmp/` and CLAUDE.md is emphatic
about that, but the harness's own scratch is not a rule a run can follow its way out of.

hooks.command: python3 -c "import importlib,subprocess,sys; need=[p for m,p in [('yaml','pyyaml'),('requests','requests')] if not importlib.util.find_spec(m)]; subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pip','install','--break-system-packages','-q',*need]) if need else None" 2>/dev/null || true
